page: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g is a general-purpose, dedicated compute cloud server within the VX1 Cloud Compute line. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, configured with 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs via multithreading. Memory provisioning stands at 256.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per core). For storage, the configuration includes 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It provides 1 complimentary public IPv4 address and features no discrete GPU hardware.

Hardware instruction set support on this AMD EPYC instance includes AVX, AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration, as well as hardware-assisted virtualization (SVM). In standardized testing, the instance registers top-tier results across Geekbench single-core (2775.0) and multi-core (25521.0) evaluations, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 98,888.12. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks reach 530.35 GB/sec for uncached reads and 259.87 GB/sec for writes, placing uncached memory throughput in the top decile.

The 64-thread allocation delivers high throughput in computationally intensive applications, demonstrating top-tier marks in PassMark database operations (41,716.12) and Clang software compilation (63,309.0). In CPU-based machine learning inference, the platform outputs 5,731.94 prompt tokens per second and 391.46 text generation tokens per second using a 135M model, transitioning to 196.46 prompt tokens per second and 38.12 text generation tokens per second on a 7B parameter model.

From an architectural standpoint, the 1 GB local NVMe SSD limits local persistent file storage, meaning external network storage volumes must be attached for data-heavy configurations. However, the high compute core density, balanced 256 GB RAM allocation, and high-bandwidth memory make the vx1-g-64c-256g suitable for distributed compilation, high-concurrency Redis caching instances, large-scale web services, relational database hosting, and medium-scale CPU inference.
description: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs backed by 32 physical cores on an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 256.0 GB of RAM and 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU supports AVX-512 extensions including BF16 and VNNI, contributing to top-tier scores in PassMark CPU tests (98,888.12) and Geekbench multi-core workloads (25,521.0). The server handles large-scale operations with strong memory throughput, generating 530.35 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. A minimal local disk footprint requires external storage integration for larger file systems. Given its 4.0 GB memory-per-core ratio and high thread concurrency, it is well suited for database engines, Redis in-memory caches, software compilation clusters, and CPU-driven machine learning inference pipelines.
